This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Strum: muted eighths, open in the chorus**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd) · [Comping rhythms](index.qmd#chords)

## The pattern

Palm-muted eighth-note downstrokes in the verse, then open down-up eighths in the Chorus bars. On guitar the chords become power chords on the low strings. With no Chorus bars set, the second half of the form is the open part.

It belongs in *Emo / pop-punk* and *Straight-eighth rock*. Here it is in the emo / pop-punk style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

## Step 1: Strum: downstrokes on the beat

Start with something simpler. One ringing downstroke on every beat. The first strum to learn, and the usual one for a slow song.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords-strum-quarters.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="emo" data-chart="C|G|Am|F" data-tempo="106" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Strum: downstrokes on the beat","opts":{"compRhythm":"strumQuarters"}}]'></div>

## Step 2: Strum: down-up eighths

Every eighth note, down on the beat and up off it, leaning on 2 and 4.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords-strum-eights.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="emo" data-chart="C|G|Am|F" data-tempo="106" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Strum: down-up eighths","opts":{"compRhythm":"strumEights"}}]'></div>

## Step 3: Strum: muted eighths, open in the chorus, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Verse: palm-muted downstrokes on every eighth, the side of the picking hand resting on the strings by the bridge. Chorus: lift the hand and play open down-up eighths. The change between them is the arrangement.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="emo" data-chart="C|G|Am|F" data-tempo="106" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Strum: muted eighths, open in the chorus","opts":{"compRhythm":"strumPunk"}},{"label":"Strum: down-up eighths (the step before)","opts":{"compRhythm":"strumEights"}}]'></div>

## Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 150 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's chord player off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="emo" data-chart="C|G|Am|F" data-tempo="150" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Strum: muted eighths, open in the chorus","opts":{"compRhythm":"strumPunk"}}]'></div>

## Step 5: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. The pattern keeps its rhythm and changes chord where the bar does: watch the staff for the hit that lands on beat 3.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="emo" data-chart="C G|Am F|C G|F G" data-tempo="150" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Strum: muted eighths, open in the chorus","opts":{"compRhythm":"strumPunk"}}]'></div>
